title: Anthropic Prices Record IPO in a Market – and World – on Edge
summary: Although we are not equity analysts, we agree with the S-1 risk factors section that the end of humanity could materially affect Anthropic’s earnings.

#### WHAT HAPPENED


**Anthropic**[completed](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-ai-offering-price.html) **the largest IPO in history on Wednesday evening, pricing at $83 per share, after updating its prospectus last week with an expected price range of $70 to $78.** Strong demand led the AI company, best known for its Claude chatbot, to upsize its offering, selling about 980 million shares and raising $81.3 billion, up from the 825 million originally planned. That figure surpasses Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which raised $75 billion when it went public in June, and Anthropic's IPO price implied a valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion for a company founded barely six years ago. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley led the deal, as they did for SpaceX. Ahead of the open, Cboe’s JJ Kinahan[said](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-opens-today-demand-seven-175239862.html) demand was running almost seven times the offering, and CNBC sources reported that retail demand was the largest in history.


Shares began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT at 11:48 a.m. ET on Thursday. The first print was $111.50, 34% above the IPO price, which briefly gave the company a market capitalization of $2 trillion. The stock hit its intraday high of $114.99 in the minute after the first trade and then spent the rest of the session fading. By the afternoon it was trading in the mid-$90s, at $94.67, up about 14% from the offering price, as of 2:18 p.m. ET. The decline from the open was unusually steep. Of 20 big US IPOs since 2008, only Coupang was doing worse at the same point in its first day, according to Yahoo Finance; the group’s average was up about 3.5%. The broader market also sold off as soon as the stock opened. Stocks fell to their session lows the moment Anthropic began trading, and chip stocks including Nvidia and Broadcom erased their gains. Listed ANT options are set to start trading on Monday.


Onchain, Hyperliquid showed the success of its[pre-IPO perp market](https://www.galaxy.com/insights/research/weekly-top-stories-05-22-26-ethereum-foundation-exits-pre-ipo-crypto-markets-fed-payment-rails) yet again. Its markets correctly called the deal pricing, with the perp trading well above the $70-78 range for weeks, signaling that demand was stronger than the underwriters’ original target. The perp ultimately undershot the open by about 7%, with the contract trading around $103.67 at 8:40 AM ET, roughly 25% above the $83/share offer price. Thursday morning’s perp price was roughly in line with market consensus (Cboe’s Kinahan[said](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-opens-today-demand-seven-175239862.html) the first trade should land around $103 or $104), but ultimately both the perps and the pros were off with the first trade ultimately printing at $111.50.


But the perp nailed where the stock ended up trading. For most of the week before listing, the perp sat in the mid-to-high $90s. It was about $96.93 as of Nov. 17 and $98.83 on the hourly chart the night before pricing, having briefly fallen below $94 during the earlier tech selloff. After the opening pop faded, the stock traded right back into that band, around $94–$97 by the afternoon. One could argue the perp’s week-long equilibrium was a better estimate of “fair” first-day value than the opening print, which looked like a short-lived demand spike.


**OUR TAKE**


There was something strange about watching Anthropic’s staff clap on the Nasdaq floor as they IPO’d a company whose primary media narrative is that AI might kill us all.


> ***Although we are not equity analysts, we agree with the S-1 risk factors section that the end of humanity*** **could** ***materially affect Anthropic’s results.***


This week has been the most *doomer* week in recent memory, coming off the back of Microsoft’s O365 outage Thursday, the nationwide FAA ground stop Friday, bank outages on Monday, even the NSA’s internal comms system reportedly disrupted (twice?). Costco[reported](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-17/costco-sees-demand-lift-from-outage-driven-stockpiling-mizuho-says) a wave of panic buying, people[pulled cash](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/19/banking-outages-emergency-cash.html) out of banks, and[prepping](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/wave-outages-americans-preparing-doomsday-121328549.html) content[went viral](https://en.tengrinews.kz/kazakhstan_news/stock-up-on-food-before-november-17-why-the-entire-internet-274610/) on social media. Chatter among traders included tips on which types of solar-powered batteries to buy, how to store substantial amounts of dry food in a New York City apartment, and which are the best routes to escape the city in the event of a grid collapse. So maybe it’s only fitting that this week’s blockbuster IPO was one in which the S-1’s risk factors[included](https://www.fortune.com/2026/10/26/anthropic-s1-risk-factors-existential-risk-pentagon-dario-amodei/) “the end of humanity.” (Although we are not equity analysts, we agree that the end of humanity *could* materially affect Anthropic’s earnings.)


Since Oct. 1, the S&P 500 is down 7%, gold is off 12.2%, and BTC is in the red 25%. Treasuries have depreciated, inflation is hot, rates are expected to rise, commodities are falling, and the Democrats swept to power largely on calls to solve the “affordability crisis.” Our own Bitcoin fear & greed index is printing near all-time lows (meaning “extreme fear”), the VIX is trading at levels comparable to those from the breakout of the Iran War in March, though not quite the level from the “Tariff Tantrum” in April 2025. Stanley Druckenmiller[said](https://x.com/TheTranscript_/status/2123163288196600167) he is “more uncertain than ever after 50 years of investing” and that his firm’s equity positions are “basically flat.” Another Wall Street luminary, Howard Marks,[argued](https://newsable.asianetnews.com/markets/howard-marks-calls-ai-exposure-a-fault-line-running-through-portfolios-highlights-nearly-600b-in-ai-related-debt-issuance-articleshow-gzqtd48) in a Nov. 11[memo](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4066318718423941) entitled “A Layman Thinks About AI” that the breakneck speed of AI development is a big risk, even for Anthropic. Paul Tudor Jones[said](https://alpha-maven.com/story/hedge-fund/billionaire-paul-tudor-jones-has-message-for-stock-market-investors-tradingview) in mid-October that “2027 is going to be a really difficult year for the stock market.” So it’s fair to say the stock market intelligentsia is uneasy.


Some have theorized that recent risk asset headwinds were enhanced by the liquidity drain caused by allocators pulling assets to buy the Anthropic IPO. This does feel intuitively right, though there’s not much evidence to directly support it. Bitcoin’s price did behave similarly when it traded poorly into the SpaceX IPO in June and made its current bear-market low on July 1 ($57,717 on Coinbase). Whether BTC and other risk assets will receive some respite now that ANT is a public stock remains to be seen.


The reality is that Americans are fearful and psychologically traumatized. Polarization has long been a characteristic of the American political landscape, but the Democratic sweep was so dramatic that big swings are expected on things like tax policy, AI policy, legislative priorities, and more. Layer on the never-ending drumbeat of cyber vulnerabilities and a spectrum of AI outcomes that is so wide it contains both the possibilities of permanent utopia and impending obliteration of the species, and it’s easy to see why markets are unsteady. There’s a sense that one more piece of big bad news could tip markets over the edge – a major cyber-attack, an escalation of the Iran or Ukraine wars, an outbreak or substantial natural disaster. Alternatively, a major peace deal or initiative emanating from Trump’s visit with Xi and Putin, cessation of major regional conflicts, or a legislative breakthrough in Congress could assuage the fears.


As they say, if you’re going through hell, keep going.[The only way out is through](https://thepoetryhour.com/poems/a-servant-to-servants/) . Everything is different, yes, but[everything is fine](https://www.galaxy.com/insights/podcasts/galaxy-brains/midterms-and-markets-with-tyler-williams) . Bitcoin keeps[producing blocks uninterrupted](https://mempool.space/) , and I just coded a slick new dashboard to monitor the situation.
